what_it_is.text: A synthetic white pigment used as a colour additive in food.

why_used.text: It makes foods appear whiter or more opaque.

explanation.text: Authorities disagree on whether titanium dioxide is safe as a food additive.

authority_positions.statement: EFSA concluded that E171 can no longer be considered safe when used as a food additive because a concern for genotoxicity could not be excluded.
FDA permits titanium dioxide as a colour additive in foods at no more than 1% by weight under 21 CFR 73.575 and did not identify genotoxicity concerns from the available data.
Health Canada found no conclusive scientific evidence that food-grade titanium dioxide is a concern for human health.

flag.flag_reason: EFSA concluded E171 is no longer safe as a food additive; the EU withdrew authorization in 2022. FDA and Health Canada still permit it.

what_it_is.text: An artificial low-calorie sweetener.

why_used.text: It adds sweetness with fewer calories than sugar.

explanation.text: IARC classified aspartame as possibly carcinogenic (Group 2B) while JECFA reaffirmed the acceptable daily intake of 0–40 mg/kg body weight.

authority_positions.statement: IARC classified aspartame as Group 2B, possibly carcinogenic to humans, based on limited evidence for hepatocellular carcinoma.
JECFA found no sufficient reason to change the acceptable daily intake of 0–40 mg/kg body weight and judged the evidence of an association with cancer in humans to be not convincing.

flag.flag_reason: IARC classified aspartame as possibly carcinogenic (Group 2B) while JECFA reaffirmed the existing acceptable daily intake as safe.

what_it_is.text: A synthetic red food colour.

why_used.text: It colours foods red.

explanation.text: FDA revoked authorization for FD&C Red No. 3 in food in January 2025.

authority_positions.statement: FDA revoked the authorization for FD&C Red No. 3 as a colour additive in food and ingested drugs, effective January 15, 2027 for compliance.

flag.flag_reason: FDA revoked authorization for FD&C Red No. 3 in food.

what_it_is.text: A synthetic red food colour.

why_used.text: It colours foods and beverages red.

explanation.text: FDA announced a plan to phase out petroleum-based synthetic dyes including Red 40 from the food supply.

authority_positions.statement: FDA announced it is working with industry to eliminate FD&C Red No. 40 from the food supply, citing concerns about children's health.

flag.flag_reason: FDA announced a phase-out of petroleum-based synthetic food dyes including FD&C Red No. 40.

what_it_is.text: A brown colour made by heating sugars.

why_used.text: It colours foods and beverages brown.

explanation.text: Caramel colour is one of the most widely used food colours.

what_it_is.text: A natural yellow-orange colour from annatto seeds.

why_used.text: It colours foods yellow to orange.

explanation.text: Annatto is a plant-derived colour commonly used in cheese and butter.

what_it_is.text: Natural pigments found in fruits and vegetables.

why_used.text: They colour foods red to blue.

explanation.text: Anthocyanins are plant pigments extracted from sources such as grape skins.

what_it_is.text: Naturally occurring compounds related to vitamin E.

why_used.text: They slow oxidation and help preserve freshness.

explanation.text: Tocopherols are antioxidants that delay rancidity in fats and oils.

what_it_is.text: Emulsifiers derived from fats.

why_used.text: They help ingredients mix and maintain a uniform texture.

explanation.text: Mono- and diglycerides are among the most common food emulsifiers.

what_it_is.text: A thickener extracted from red seaweed.

why_used.text: It thickens and stabilizes foods.

explanation.text: Carrageenan is a seaweed-derived additive used for texture in dairy products and beverages.

what_it_is.text: A mineral compound used as a food additive.

why_used.text: It can serve as a white colour, an acidity regulator, or a calcium supplement in foods.

explanation.text: Calcium carbonate is a common mineral additive with multiple functions in food.

what_it_is.text: A phosphate salt used as a food additive.

why_used.text: It can regulate acidity and act as an emulsifier in processed foods.

explanation.text: Trisodium phosphate is a buffering and emulsifying agent found in cereals and processed cheese.

what_it_is.text: A protein derived from animal collagen.

why_used.text: It thickens and gels foods.

explanation.text: Gelatin gives a gel-like texture to desserts, yogurts, and confections.

what_it_is.text: An organic acid naturally found in fruits.

why_used.text: It adds tartness and controls acidity.

explanation.text: Malic acid is an acidulant that gives a tart taste to candy and fruit-flavoured foods.

what_it_is.text: The sodium salt of citric acid.

why_used.text: It controls acidity and acts as an emulsifying salt.

explanation.text: Sodium citrate is a buffering agent used in dairy products and beverages.

what_it_is.text: A natural thickener from carob tree seeds.

why_used.text: It thickens and stabilizes food texture.

explanation.text: Locust bean gum is a plant-derived thickener used in ice cream and dairy products.

what_it_is.text: The sodium salt of benzoic acid, used as a preservative.

why_used.text: It inhibits microbial growth in acidic foods.

explanation.text: Sodium benzoate is a preservative effective in acidic foods such as soft drinks and pickles.

what_it_is.text: The potassium salt of sorbic acid, used as a preservative.

why_used.text: It inhibits mold and yeast growth in foods.

explanation.text: Potassium sorbate is a preservative commonly used in cheese, baked goods, and beverages.

what_it_is.text: A polysaccharide produced by bacterial fermentation.

why_used.text: It thickens and stabilizes foods.

explanation.text: Xanthan gum is a widely used thickener and stabilizer in sauces, dressings, and gluten-free baking.

what_it_is.text: An artificial sweetener derived from sugar.

why_used.text: It adds sweetness without calories.

explanation.text: Sucralose is a high-intensity sweetener about 600 times sweeter than sugar.

what_it_is.text: An artificial high-intensity sweetener.

why_used.text: It adds sweetness without calories.

explanation.text: Acesulfame potassium is often used in combination with other sweeteners.

what_it_is.text: A salt used as a curing agent and preservative in meat products.

why_used.text: It preserves colour and inhibits bacterial growth in cured meats.

explanation.text: Sodium nitrite is a regulated preservative used in meat curing with maximum permitted levels.
